Standard: Multiple systems are physically separated IAW SAE AS5440B, System Separation paragraph, to prevent loss of SCFs due to damage. Hydraulic and pneumatic lines will have a minimum separation of 0.25-inch, IAW SAE AS5440B, Tubing Clearance paragraph, with adjacent structure, tubing, and other installations. Positive separation from wiring is IAW SAE AS50881H, Gas and Fluid Carrying Lines and Tubes paragraph. Clearances are maintained under all operating conditions, environments, tolerance stack-up, and installation preloads to avoid problems such as binding, chafing or jamming. Hydraulic lines (including hoses, drains, and vents) are separated and routed below all ignition sources (e.g., exhaust stacks, electrical wiring, avionics, and insulating materials) to prevent risk of fire from line leakage. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Review system-level drawings or CAD models to verify that specified tubing and hose clearances are designed into the system.
(2) Review results of a quality assessment or a government in-person sampling of physical inspection(s) (e.g., 30-60-90% of build inspections) of the air vehicle to verify minimum hydraulic and pneumatic line separation is maintained. Demonstration.
  (1) Conduct air vehicle functional checkout of tubing and flexible hose installations to verify that clearances are maintained throughout the whole range of motion and under worst-case environmental conditions (e.g., cold soak, hot soak, and air vehicle vibrations and loading). The effects of actuation, loading, and line movement will also be observed as system is exercised to verify line clearances are maintained to prevent chafing of lines and kinking of hoses. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Examination.
(3) Conduct visual inspection of hoses, tubing, and any adjacent lines, components, or structure after flight test to verify there is no evidence of contact (e.g., chafing).
